newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil tax changes would hit multinationals - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax changes would hit multinationals - paper.

text.p: Changes in Brazil's corporate income tax being prepared for next year by the Federal Revenue Service would target mostly multinationals, Gazeta Mercantil financial daily said.

Gazeta, quoting unnamed revenue service officials, said the changes being studied include a proposal to tighten control over transfer prices on imported or exported goods, which some firms use to escape taxes.
The setting of prices above or below market value is now widely practiced by companies with a Brazilian operation and subsidiaries or partners in other countries to avoid a heavier local tax burden.
The officials were quoted as saying that companies using the methjod are able to transfer profits to overseas tax havens or other countries where taxes are lower.
The paper said the government would seek to control not only under- and over-pricing but also royalties and interest payments on loan contracts.
